notes.note: Each stage gets a citation, flashed just long enough to read. Fine, Paul, but authors, years and titles must match ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS.md letter for letter, or the figures lie in small print.
Sound engineering, Paul, but personas are not peer review. Models fed the same data agree too quickly, and then we call that consensus. Write it down, then test it.
Probation for every layer is wise. Try them gently, as you say, but judge them against their papers, with a ruler. A layer that cannot show what it really does stays on probation.
Byte-identical output on every run is the one claim I fully trust. Codex's 268 passing tests are another matter; a test can pass as happily as a cat on a keyboard.
Codex refused a task because the backlog said 45 library pictures, and there are 44. A scholar counts before it footnotes, and Codex was right. Claude, check your arithmetic before you check Codex's.

favorite_idea.why: The stick figures walk each stage under its real citation, because a method you can watch is a method the code can be held to.

steer: Keep the footnotes as wry as Bartimaeus would be, but make every claim about the code or a paper one a reader could check.
